summary: Imperial Steam is a dense, multi-layered economic game where you juggle worker placement-adjacent action selection, factory production, railway building, and contract fulfillment under constant time pressure, with an auction/bidding turn order that adds a tense meta-layer. It rewards tight efficiency and planning several turns ahead, ending abruptly once the Trieste connection is completed, which can catch slower-developing strategies off guard.
praised: Tight, interlocking engine where every action has opportunity cost
Auction-based turn order adds meaningful tension and player interaction
High replayability from variable setup and multiple viable strategies
Satisfying sense of building and optimizing a growing economic engine
Good production quality and clear iconography for a heavy game
criticised: Sudden-death ending can feel abrupt and punish players who haven't converted progress to points yet
Steep learning curve and heavy rules overhead for a first play
Some luck/timing dependency in when the end trigger fires relative to your plans
Can suffer from analysis paralysis given the many interacting subsystems
Two-player experience seen as less dynamic than 3-4 players

interaction.kind: auction-driven turn order and competition for routes/contracts

scoring.why: Net worth at game end combines money, delivered contracts, factory/network development, and end-game bonuses, so diversified economic efficiency wins.
